Inspect databases, roles, schemas, and tables

PostgreSQL 19.0

Type these commands inside psql after connecting. Backslash commands are processed by the psql client and end at Enter. SQL statements such as SELECT are sent to the server and normally end with a semicolon.

Where am I connected?

The connection summary shows the current database, role, and connection address or socket.

\conninfo

List databases

Shows the databases on this server. Look for learning_db after creating it. The columns and values can vary with your psql and server versions and locale settings.

\l
Name
The database name, such as learning_db.
Owner
The role that owns the database.
Encoding
The character encoding. UTF8 supports Burmese text.
Locale Provider
Where the database gets its locale behavior. Examples include libc (operating system), icu, and builtin (PostgreSQL).
Collate
The locale setting for comparing and sorting text.
Ctype
The locale setting for character classification and case conversion.
Locale
The locale identifier for providers that use this field, such as ICU. It may be blank for libc.
ICU Rules
Custom ICU collation rules, if configured.
Access privileges
Explicit database privileges for roles, such as CONNECT or CREATE. A blank cell can mean the built-in defaults apply.

Count the databases

This SQL query counts the database entries on the connected server, including template databases.

SELECT count(*) AS database_count FROM pg_database;

List roles

The Role name column contains role names. The Attributes column summarizes the special settings of each role. The built-in administrator on a typical local installation may show the attributes below. Run \du postgres to inspect just that role.

\du
Superuser
Bypasses database permission checks except the right to log in.
Create role
Can create roles and manage eligible roles it administers.
Create DB
Can create databases.
Replication
Can start streaming replication when its login and connection rules also allow it.
Bypass RLS
Bypasses row-level security policies, which can otherwise restrict access to individual rows.
LOGIN / Cannot login
LOGIN lets a role authenticate if its connection rules allow it. A role without LOGIN can still group privileges.

What to expect Example row: postgres | Superuser, Create role, Create DB, Replication, Bypass RLS

List schemas

Shows schemas in the current database. A schema is a namespace for objects such as tables. The examples use the usual public schema.

\dn

List visible tables

Shows tables visible from the current schema search path. Run \dt public.* to explicitly list tables in public. If the database is empty, there may be no tables to show.

\dt

Inspect a table’s columns and constraints

After creating courses in the setup lesson, this displays its columns, data types, defaults, and constraints. Replace courses with the table you want to inspect.

\d courses

Check the connected server version

The SQL function version() reports the server version. In your OS terminal, psql --version reports the client version.

SELECT version();

Find help or exit

Try these one at a time. Use \q last because it returns you to the operating-system terminal. If command output opens in a pager, press q by itself to close the pager and stay in psql.

\?
\h SELECT
\q
\?
Lists psql backslash commands.
\h SELECT
Shows syntax help for the SQL SELECT statement.
\q
Closes psql and returns to your terminal.
